points.title: Fed drafts stablecoin issuer rulebook
points.detail: Two proposals under the 2025 GENIUS Act set reserve limits and capital standards for Fed-supervised payment stablecoin issuers, now open for public comment.

knowledge.title_en: Stablecoin Reserves vs Capital Under the GENIUS Act
knowledge.body_en:
The GENIUS Act, signed in July 2025, created the first US federal license for payment stablecoins. Issuers must hold reserves of at least 1:1 in cash, insured deposits, short Treasury bills or Treasury repo, disclose them monthly, and may not pay interest to holders. Issuers above $10 billion outstanding move from state to federal supervision.

The Fed's two proposals fill in what the statute left open: how much capital an issuer needs on top of reserves, and limits on what the reserves may contain. Reserves back the coins; capital absorbs losses when reserves slip below par, for example if a bank holding deposits fails. That gap is what broke stablecoin pegs in 2023.
knowledge.why_en: The Fed's proposals set the rulebook that Tether, Circle and any bank entrant must meet to issue payment stablecoins in the US.
